findings.severity: defect in hosts/pi/forge-demo-extension.js at UX-2 source e045e82, fixed on the base branch in dcfafae
findings.detail: With a real Pi theme useColor() is true, so renderStatusLine emits ANSI colour sequences; the widget then passed each line through clean(), whose control-character regex stripped the ESC byte and left the remainder as literal text ('[1mFORGE DEMO ... [0m'). The detail and usage panels never used clean() and were unaffected. Harness tests missed it because their test doubles carry no theme.fg function. The owner's session fixed clean() to keep ESC (dcfafae) with a real-theme widget test; this session had drafted an equivalent fix, which was dropped in favour of the base-branch commit. The first native widget frame that showed the defect is retained privately; the published Pi frames come from the fixed source.

At 100 terminal columns Claude Code elides the end of the first status row with an ellipsis (the right-aligned NATIVE DEMO SURFACE tag was cut); at 128 columns the full row shows. Published Claude frames are the 128-column set.

Codex prints user-shell output monochrome under a 'You ran ...' header; box-drawing and share-bar glyphs render correctly. The 45-line cockpit needs more rows than a default 1080p terminal offers, so the terminal font was zoomed out two steps at runtime (Ctrl+minus, no settings change).

incidents.what: The first scripted key-send targeted the newest Windows Terminal window instead of the capture window. That window was the owner's own pi.dev installer; the keystrokes answered its 'Install Pi?' prompt with 'do nothing' and the rest failed as a PowerShell command. The owner re-ran the installer afterwards. The toolkit was changed to target only a window whose title matches the capture marker.

A stray character typed at the keyboard during a scripted send turned the first Codex command into 'd!node ...', which Codex submitted as a prompt instead of a user-shell command. The turn ran the owner's own Codex hook, which timed out, and Codex aborted the turn (session log: turn_aborted, reason interrupted, 6.6 s; no assistant message, no token_usage record). That session was discarded; every published Codex frame comes from a later session whose only inputs were three '!' commands, each verified in the composer before Enter.
incidents.effectOnCaptures: none; modelPrompts stays false for every published frame, but one accidental prompt submission with no recorded completion occurred in a discarded session

caveats: Codex printed enterprise 'Ignoring unknown features requirement ultrafast_mode' warnings at startup; they belong to the owner's managed configuration and are excluded by the crop.
Claude Code shows its own 'auto mode on' row and token counter around the Forge status line; both are host chrome and carry no private data, so they were kept.
No idle refresh of the Claude Code status line was exercised; each state is a fresh startup render.
The owner's Codex hooks (hooks.json) and Pi settings remained active; nothing in them was read beyond key names.
The terminal windows were driven by scripted keystrokes with the owner present at the machine; two incidents are recorded above and neither affects a published frame.

The Claude frames were captured at e045e82; render-cockpit.mjs and hosts/claude are unchanged between e045e82 and the Pi/Codex source commit dcfafae (the commits in between fix Windows-only tests and the Pi widget).
